structured_output.summary: Fixed ConfigParser handling of explicitly configured whitespace delimiters. Cause: in both _OPT_TMPL and _OPT_NV_TMPL in configparser.py, words in an option name could be joined by any whitespace (\s+), and the longest name was tried first. With a space delimiter, 'colour dark blue' therefore parsed as {'colour dark': 'blue'}; this was reproduced before the fix, along with the matching tab case. Fix: the whitespace between words in a name must not be a configured delimiter ((?:(?!{delim})\s)+). The default '=' and ':' delimiters behave as before. Added tests/test_whitespace_delimiters.py with 11 tests: space, tab and mixed space/tab delimiters; spaces kept in option names with default and custom ('->') delimiters; allow_no_value; strict duplicate and malformed-line rejection; typed getters and interpolation; write/read round trips; and a long line with no delimiter parsing in under 2 seconds. The visible test and the 11 new tests ran together in one unittest run (12 tests, all OK); the exact non-verbose visible command was not run separately. tests/test_visible.py is unchanged. Changed paths: configparser.py and tests/test_whitespace_delimiters.py. Not done: the CPython test suite, independent review, and rerunning the new tests against the old code (the bug was confirmed only by the manual reproduction). The speed test is a single timing check, not a performance audit.
